failure_location.quote: by introducing a larger eigen gap, which in turn reduces the number of restarts required in the Arnoldi restarting iterative method

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\sum_{i=1}^n H_{i\ell} = |\bm{C}_\ell|$
and $C = D^{-\tfrac12}F$
Apply $k$-means clustering to the rows of $H = D^{-1/2} X$

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:added-1 shows F^TH=0 encodes fairness only when H is a (scaled) cluster indicator. In the L_sym relaxation, the orthonormal variable is X = D^{1/2}H_ind, so fairness reads (D^{-1/2}F)^T X = 0, exactly as the paper's own S-Fair-SC section uses. Problem (mainobj) instead imposes F^TX=0, which corresponds to F^T D^{1/2} H_ind = 0. That is not the balance condition unless degrees are constant. Fair-SMW (sym) is built on this problem and clusters rows of H without rescaling.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace F by C = D^{-1/2}F in (mainobj) and in Fair-SMW-sym, and apply k-means to D^{-1/2}H; then re-run the affected experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The fair normalized-cut relaxation that Fair-SMW-sym claims to solve is mis-specified, so it does not target the stated group-fairness constraint.
issues.title: Fair objective imposes F^TH=0 on the L_sym embedding instead of the indicator variable
issues.why_classification: The repair changes the formulation and the algorithm and invalidates the reported runs, but stays within the existing framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $Z \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times (n-h+1)}$ denote an orthonormal basis for the null space of $F^T$.
Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.failure_explanation: Z is n x (n-h+1), so it is not invertible and ZZ^T is not I. Hence (Z^TGZ)^{-1} differs from Z^TG^{-1}Z in general. The final U = G - GF(F^TGF)^{-1}F^TG equals Z(Z^TG^{-1}Z)^{-1}Z^T, so Fair-SMW returns Z times the bottom eigenvectors of Z^TG^{-1}Z, not the top eigenvectors of Z^TGZ. Counterexample with n=3, F=e3, Z=[e1,e2], G=[[2,0,1.9],[0,1.5,0],[1.9,0,2]] (SPD): Z^TGZ=diag(2,1.5) has top eigenvector e1. Z^TG^{-1}Z is approximately diag(5.13,0.667), whose bottom eigenvector is e2.

failure_location.quote: using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either redefine the method as solving the different problem (SMW2) and justify that objective, or replace U with an operator whose top eigenvectors are those of Z^TGZ.
issues.overall_effect: Fair-SMW (all variants) does not solve the fair spectral problem (SMW1)/(mainobj) as claimed. The claimed solution equivalence with Fair-SC/S-Fair-SC fails except when GF lies in range(F).
issues.title: False equivalence of (SMW1) and (SMW2) via Z^T = Z^{-1} for non-square Z
issues.why_classification: The core reformulation underlying the method is invalid, and its central guarantee (same optimizer as fair SC) is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal{L}(H, \Lambda, \mu) = \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}(H^T G^{-1} H) - \text{Tr}(\Lambda^T (F^T H)) - \frac{\mu}{2} \|F^T H\|_F^2
\min_{H} \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}\left(H^T \left( G^{-1} - \mu F F^T \right) H \right)

issues.failure_explanation: For a minimization problem, the penalty -mu/2||F^TH||^2 rewards constraint violation. The derivation consistently yields G^{-1} - mu FF^T, whose minimizers move into range(F) as mu grows. (SMW3) then silently switches to G^{-1} + mu FF^T, which does not follow from the displayed derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the standard +mu/2||F^TH||_F^2 penalty and redo the gradient and subproblem with the + sign.
issues.overall_effect: The penalty formulation underlying Fair-SMW is not supported by its derivation as written.
issues.title: Augmented Lagrangian penalty has wrong sign; derived matrix contradicts (SMW3)
issues.why_classification: A routine sign correction aligns the derivation with (SMW3) and leaves the rest unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we need $G$ to be invertible, and we need $U$ to have real eigenvalues.
For $G_{\text{sym}}$ and $G_{\text{aff}}$, it is clear that symmetry holds.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation needs G positive definite (thm:added-1 hypothesis, min/max inversion, and invertibility of F^TGF). Theorems are proved only for G_sym and G_rw. For a weighted W this can fail: with n=2 and edge weight 2, G_aff=[[2,2],[2,2]] is singular.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume weights in [0,1] with zero diagonal and use Gershgorin to get lambda_min(W+nI) >= 1, or shift by max degree plus one.
issues.overall_effect: AFF-Fair-SMW, the headline variant, is not shown to be well defined for the stated input class of weighted adjacency matrices.
issues.title: Invertibility/positivity of G_aff = W + nI never established; fails for general weights
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis plus a one-line bound restores all claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is a symmetric matrix (implying $G$ is also symmetric and invertible)
For $G_{\text{rw}}$, we do not have the property of symmetry

issues.failure_explanation: The Fair-SMW derivation explicitly assumes symmetric G. It relies on that assumption for the gradient G^{-1}H, for the identification of trace optima with eigenvectors, and for the min-over-A/max-over-A^{-1} step. For nonsymmetric G_rw, Tr(H^TGH) depends only on the symmetric part of G, so the top eigenvectors of the nonsymmetric U_rw solve none of the stated trace problems.

failure_location.quote: we can construct two alternative algorithms by substituting $G_{\text{sym}}$ with either $G_{\text{rw}} = D^{-1} W + 2 I$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the derivation to symmetric G, and either drop the RW variant or present it as a heuristic (or recast it via a D-weighted symmetric formulation).
issues.title: RW variant uses nonsymmetric G_rw in a derivation that requires symmetric G
issues.why_classification: One variant loses its justification; the symmetric variants are unaffected, so the loss is limited.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$

issues.failure_explanation: Real eigenvalues in [-1,1] do not bound the quadratic form of the nonsymmetric D^{-1}W. For the path P3, the symmetric part B has eigenvalue 3*sqrt(2)/4 > 1. For a star with 100 leaves and x=(1,-0.1,...,-0.1): x^TD^{-1}Wx = -10.1 and x^Tx = 2, so x^TG_rw x = -6.1 < 0. The positivity claim is false; only the real-eigenvalue part holds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the positivity claim and replace it with positivity in the D-inner product (x^T D G_rw x = x^T(W+2D)x > 0), then rework its use for the RW variant.
issues.overall_effect: The hypothesis of thm:added-1 is not available for G_rw, so invertibility of G_rw^{-1}+mu FF^T and of F^TG_rwF is unsupported.
issues.title: G_rw is not positive definite: numerical range of D^{-1}W is not bounded by 1
issues.why_classification: The stated property is false, but a comparable D-weighted version survives with a short new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Right-multiplication preserves the column space, not the row space. The identity requires D^{-1}range(F) to lie in range(F), which fails in general. Counterexample: path 1-2-3 with V1={v1}, so F=(1,-1/2,-1/2)^T and D=diag(1,2,1). The left side is (1,-0.25,-0.5), but the right side is about (0.917,-0.458,-0.458). The simplification of P and the symmetry of the resulting W-script P therefore collapse.

failure_location.quote: multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove real spectrum of U_rw by a valid argument or redefine U_rw (e.g., with a D-weighted constraint) so that it is similar to a symmetric matrix.
issues.overall_effect: The real-eigenvalue guarantee for U_rw, and thus the well-posedness of RW-Fair-SMW's top-eigenvector step, is unsupported. U_rw is in general similar only to an oblique, nonsymmetric product.
issues.title: False identity F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} P_F underpins proof of real spectrum of U_rw
issues.why_classification: The key step is false and no alternative argument is available, so the theorem must be abandoned or replaced.
